verdicts.rewritten_summary: Outright International country overview (last updated 12 March 2026): same-sex intimacy legal but very few protections — hate crimes and hate speech on sexual orientation are penalised, while discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity is not banned (reported discrimination is described as rare); same-sex couples have no marriage or adoption, and LGBTIQ visibility in the principality is limited.

French gay travel guide Monaco page: no gay Pride is held anywhere in Monaco (visitors are sent to France or Italy for one); the ~200-hectare state is pitched as a luxury/relaxation destination with an LGBTQ+-welcoming accommodation directory but no discernible local scene.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Nice-Matin via Monaco Haut Commissariat (March 2025, French): homosexuality decriminalised since the 18th century, yet Monaco ranks near the bottom of European LGBT-rights rankings — no equal succession, survivor pensions or parental leave for same-sex partners; roughly 10 people dare to be openly out; Council of Europe rapporteur Béatrice Fresko-Rolfo: "C’est le triste bilan de Monaco".

Queer In The World Monaco guide (updated 3 December 2023): homosexuality legal and SOGI discrimination illegal only in certain contexts — limited protections with room for improvement; advises visitors to stay current with local laws and customs.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023), Moldova: a trans woman was denied bank service over a document/appearance mismatch and the Equality Council confirmed discrimination, recommending preventive measures; hate speech remained serious with no meaningful state response (echoed in the European Commission country report); election-period political hate speech rose.

Amnesty International Moldova 2025: discrimination against LGBTI people remained commonplace and freedom of expression and assembly was arbitrarily restricted (impunity for past violations); in Russian-occupied Transnistria new legislation prohibits promotion of "non-traditional sexual relations".

GENDERDOC-M report (2023) citing the Equality Council study "Prejudices and Marginalization in Moldova 2022" (published January 2023): acceptance of LGBT+ people is extremely low — 79% would not accept LGBT+ neighbours, 60% not as work colleagues (social-distance 5.7), and marginalisation of LGBT+ people increased in 2022.

Attitude (2 February 2026) revisiting Moldova Pride 2024: participants of all ages and backgrounds joined the festivities — a country "slowly emerging from its past to carve a new queer identity"; public Pride proceeds openly.

ECOM legislative analysis on SOGI and HIV in Moldova (Tallinn, 2024): identifies legal barriers affecting LGBT people and people living with HIV — access to justice, hate-crime and discrimination provisions — based on a survey of local partners, benchmarked against international standards.

PinkNews (19 May 2018): police deployed tear gas against anti-LGBT protesters trying to disrupt the annual Moldova Pride solidarity march in Chisinau (19 May) as marchers carried foam hearts; activists feared a repeat of earlier violent scenes.

PinkNews (1 March 2013): the Balti Court of Appeals ruled on 28 February that the northern city’s "gay propaganda" ban was unconstitutional and violated human rights — local church-led bans struck down after protests against the EU-backed anti-discrimination law.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: BBC News Pidgin overview of decriminalisation in Africa (July 2020): Madagascar entry — same-sex activity legal only from age 21 under the Penal Code (under-21 same-sex acts remain offences); no recognition of same-sex marriage or civil unions; regional context as ~22 of 53 African states had moved to decriminalise.

Queer In The World Madagascar guide (updated 3 December 2023): same-sex activity legal for over-21s but LGBT people face discrimination and lack civic rights such as marriage and adoption; the legal framework is limited in progress compared with other countries.

Erasing 76 Crimes (17 July 2025): in Madagascar’s fourth UPR (January 2025, 235 recommendations) the government rejected UN recommendations to combat anti-LGBT violence and hate speech and to equalise the age of consent; six Malagasy organisations (Queer Place, Mifoha Olo Mazoto, Divers’ Unité, Justice Égalitaire, Men Engage, Madagascar LGBT+) protested that "Refusing to act is to endorse impunity and condone violence."

Rights in Exile (AsyLex) Madagascar resources: Penal Code Article 331 sets a different age of consent for same-sex acts (indecent-assault band of five to ten years’ imprisonment); documents general societal discrimination against LGBTQI+ people plus state-protection capacity, case law and supporting organisations.

HRMI Maldives Summary Report 2024 (second expert survey): human-rights experts most commonly identified LGBTQIA+ people — alongside migrants, human-rights defenders, journalists, religious minorities and sex workers — as at risk of empowerment-rights violations; political participation scores relatively better at 6.4/10 while other civil and political rights score considerably lower.

Erasing 76 Crimes (1 September 2015): police on Dhaandhoo arrested two men (aged 56 and 27) on 29 August for homosexual activity in their private home; the 2014 Penal Code extended criminalisation beyond Muslims to everyone, with death-penalty provisions theoretically in reach; Rainbow Warriors warned tourists could face similar threats.

UN OHCHR compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/22/MDV/2, March 2015) for the Maldives’ second-cycle UPR: records ICCPR/CEDAW/CRC reservations and concerns including sharia-based treatment of children born outside marriage; the Human Rights Committee recommended anti-discrimination legislation covering sexual orientation and action against stigmatisation of homosexuals.

Maldives national UPR report (A/HRC/WG.6/22/MDV/1, April 2015): the government’s own submission — of 126 first-cycle recommendations it fully accepted 89, partially accepted 11, took note of 6 and rejected 20 with reasons; reports full implementation of 58 and partial implementation of 32 over four years.

HRW dispatch (31 March 2025) "Trans Rights in Mexico: Progress and Challenges": calls on Mexico’s states to guarantee administrative legal gender recognition — many states now have LGR procedures, but without recognition, document requests expose trans people to discrimination, violence and humiliation; implementation gaps persist state to state.

HRW report "I Just Want to Contribute to Society" (6 March 2024), Tabasco: barriers to legal name/gender recognition leave trans people exposed — document mismatch amplifies daily discrimination, set against murders including a trans woman found in the Carrizal River in August 2023.

The Guardian (18 July 2024): Mexico City’s Congress approved the "Paola Buenrostro law" criminalising transfemicide — a watershed named for a trans woman murdered in 2016 whose case remains unpunished; activists say the law is critical for feeling safe.

IACHR press release (2024): urges federal and Mexican state authorities to step up efforts to prevent and punish violence against trans people, demanding investigation of all LGBTI violations with gender-identity-respecting methods; warns impunity may reach alarming levels.

LSE USAPP analysis by Caroline Beer (22 November 2024): Mexico’s progressive LGBTQ+ legislation is rarely enforced fairly or uniformly — rights exist formally but are rarely enjoyed in practice; the authors explicitly caution their earlier work must not be read as evidence LGBTQ+ people are safe from state or private violence including murder and torture.

Global Affairs Canada travel advice for Mexico: "Exercise a high degree of caution" nationwide due to high levels of criminal activity and kidnapping, with regional "avoid non-essential travel" advisories (e.g. Baja California Sur and the northwestern mainland coast); recently updated for Hurricane Polo.

Intrepid Travel LGBTQIA+ Mexico guide: same-sex marriage legalised in 2009 with Mexico City the pioneer and Zona Rosa its gay hub (annual Pride, LGBT-friendly hotels/bars/tours); Cancún is a mainstream hotspot; notes Oaxaca’s indigenous muxé third-gender tradition and advises caution outside tourist hubs.

CNN en Español (19 July 2024): Mexico City’s Congress approved the "Paola Buenrostro" law criminalising transfeminicide; Transgender Europe monitoring records 593 transfeminicidios in Mexico from 2008 to September 2021, and 52 between October 2022 and September 2023 — second only to Brazil’s 100.

Mail & Guardian (13 January 2007): Coahuila became the third Latin American jurisdiction to approve gay civil unions (20–13 vote) after Mexico City and Buenos Aires, barring adoption and custody for those couples; PRI deputy Julieta Lopez called it "a sensible response" to discrimination, PAN called it an attack on the family.

Human Dignity Trust global criminalisation history: lists the Marshall Islands among the states that decriminalised same-sex conduct in the 2000s — "Marshall Islands (2005)" alongside USA (2003), Cape Verde (2004) and San Marino (2004) — i.e. no current criminalisation regime there.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Pacific Sexual & Gender Diversity Network Marshall Islands page: profiles Anfernee Nenol Kaminaga ("Nenol"), 25, a pansexual genderqueer Marshallese who co-created and led "Brighten the Rainbow", known as the first openly LGBTIQ initiative in the Marshall Islands; also a UNESCO Youth Ambassador and youth representative at the first UN Youth Climate Action Summit.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023), North Macedonia: hate speech remained serious with countless reports and no meaningful state response (European Commission country report concurs); in September the Basic Criminal Court of Skopje sentenced a man to two years for assaulting an LGBTI activist with SOGI aggravating grounds of the Criminal Code; ECRI called for a ban on nonconsensual intersex surgeries.

Global Voices (30 March 2024): TransFormA’s March for Visibility of Trans People in Skopje marked Transgender Day of Visibility — "we march bravely" — while noting a worrisome trend of mobilising religious institutions to scapegoat this small vulnerable group.

ILGA-Europe/ERA LGBTI Enlargement Review 2024 (covering 2023), North Macedonia chapter with the National Network against Homophobia and Transphobia: top priority is Legal Gender Recognition — the government withdrew the Draft Law on Civil Registry containing the LGR chapter a day before Parliamentary Committee review.

Washington Blade (13 October 2023): economic analysis with Serbian and North Macedonian LGBTI groups quantifying how anti-LGBTQ discrimination harms the economies of Serbia and North Macedonia — discrimination cast as a measurable drag on growth and jobs, without country-specific figures in the piece.

Balkan Insight (February 2012): ILGA-Europe’s Rainbow Europe Index ranked Macedonia worst in the Balkans at −2 on the 17-to−7 scale — the only Balkan country in the "red zone" of gross human-rights violations and discrimination.

Balkan Insight (July 2014): the government submitted a constitutional motion defining marriage strictly as a union of one man and one woman — ruling out same-sex marriage and adoption — as an early act of the re-elected Gruevski government, needing two-thirds of MPs with the conservative DPA expected to supply the extra votes.

Human Rights Watch (6 November 2024): Mali’s new penal code criminalises same-sex conduct with harsh penalties; previously legal but vague "public indecency" provisions (Article 225) were used against LGBT people and gender-nonconforming expressions, and the new law bans the undefined "promotion" of homosexuality, greatly expanding who can be prosecuted.

The Conversation (15 January 2025), interview with anthropologist Christophe Broqua: Mali’s new penal code — announced October 2024, in force 13 December 2024 — criminalises homosexuality and any citizen seen to encourage it, a sharp escalation under the military junta alongside clampdowns on opposition and media.
